key_insight: The paper shows that biomedical AI explanations can be made machine-checkable by linking each claim to explicit radiomic evidence, separate from prediction accuracy.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging workflows, this could help audit whether AI-generated statements about glioblastoma are actually supported by the patient’s MRI-derived data.
method: Aligned UPenn-GBM radiomics with de novo CaPTk extraction from standardized MRI and expert-validated segmentations.
Built a neuro-semantic verification framework with 1,728 MRI features across T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR in three tumor regions.
Tested transportability, provenance, deterministic claim checking, controlled performance degradation, and a small LLM claim-extraction pilot.
evidence_signal: Across 611 reference cases and an external multicenter cohort, the verifier reached 100% exact-set accuracy on 6,620 corrupted claims and maintained perfect verification even as model ROC AUC dropped from 0.899 to 0.500.
watch_item: The framework verifies consistency, not clinical truth, so implementation still depends on robust feature standardization and reliable upstream segmentation.
paper_title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
